title: Capacity-Price Coupling: Sprint KPI & Budget Notes (Jun 2026)

financial_estimates_snippet:
Quick calcs (scratch):
- Marginal cost (hosted) baseline: $28 per M tokens (infrastructure, inference ops, infra overhead).
- Dedicated reserved marginal cost (amortized): $14 per M tokens at 80% utilization.
- If reserved conversion increases by +10ppts, blended marginal cost falls by ~4.5% -> unit cost improvement.
- Hiring cost: average fully-burdened engineer = $230k/year (~$19.2k/month). Adding 6 hires (Aug–Sep) = ~$115k/month run-rate incremental opex in steady state.
- Runway sensitivity: with current burn, incremental hiring schedule reduces runway by ~2.1 months unless offset by reserved contract revenue or price increases.
- Example: a -6% promo to boost reserved sales needs ~+22% conversion lift to be NPV-neutral over 12 months (assumes 12-month commit recovery).

body:
Context / purpose:
This doc collates sprint-level budget thinking: how to phase HC and small-budget pricing experiments so that we preserve runway while testing reservation-led pricing. The goal for this sprint is not a final plan but to expose KPIs and trigger thresholds that product, ops and finance can agree on.

Top-level questions (working):
- What price windows can we test without violating existing commit SLA expectations?
- How many hires are essential for Q4 throughput targets vs optional? (we split hires into essential vs stretch)
- What is the reservation promo payback window (6 months? 12 months?) — need modeling on churn-adjusted LTV.

Rough KPI triggers (proposal):
- If reserved conversion lift > 15% in first 8 weeks post-promo, scale reserved promo to additional regions.
- If blended unit cost improves by > 6% from reserved mix shift within 3 months, accelerate hiring of 2 more runtime engineers.
- If demand falls > 18% vs baseline for two consecutive weeks after price increase, rollback price and initiate customer support outreach.

Microbudget table (scratch):
- Promo budget (Q3 test): $120k total (credits + marketing + onboarding support)
- Additional infra cushion for burst capacity in test months: $45k
- Recruiting budget ramp (Q3–Q4): $90k (recruiter fees + signing)

Open data sources:
- Billing ingestion (per-route token mix) — FIN-4321 (see linked Jira)
- Model mix telemetry (prod metrics team) — need export for elasticity stratification

Risks/notes:
- Over-indexing on short-term elasticity can undercount churn — reserved commit marketing may artificially inflate near-term conversion but lead to higher churn if onboarding poor.
- GPU spot volatility could widen our reserved vs hosted delta, affecting scenario outcomes; include 95th percentile spot run in next TCO run.

Next steps (this sprint):
- Finance: build scenario workbook with monthly cash flows and HC burn overlays (Jun 18)
- Product/PM: finalize A/B design for price/promo (Jun 22)
- Eng/Infra: finalize infra cushion plan and worst-case cost cap (Jun 25)

Notes to self: preserve this doc as the sprint log for decisions; update with links to the scenario workbook and A/B playbook once available.

-- A.P.
